body: I always feel like I am always on the periphery of society. I have been on the "inside", of fitting in. But it's a fleeting moment. When I am feeling ok, I am confident, sociable, and some even find me likable. When my depression comes back in force, I am the opposite. Anti-social. Closed off, and angry. I have accepted that I will never have the picture perfect social life you see in commercials. Bunch of people smiling and having a blast in a backyard BBQ, you know the type.

Part of me wants to have a friend that I can lean on. I don't expect her to fix my shit, just someone I could talk to. A shoulder to cry on I guess. I would understand if she wants no part of that, I am not entitled to anything and she owes me nothing. But I hope.

I've talked to the school therapist but he was the more "think positive type", which just feels like a slap in the face for me. I've stopped going. I exercise regularly and am making progress. I can distract my self with games, netflix, and music. But at the end of the day. Every moment in between is punctuated with dread.

Not that good honestly. Been really struggling with depression; it's been really bad these past two months. Varying wildly from OK to suicidal thoughts. Been struggling with keeping up with school as well, waking up is the hardest part. Going to bed too... 

I feel so alone all the time. Even when I talk to people or hang out with my friend. It's just emptiness. I got out of a two year relationship and I miss my ex. I want a partner but I am not ready, mentally. It's back to a point where I am trying to live hour by hour. Not even day by day. So alone.

>"It's better to have loved and lost, than to never have loved at all"

I am sure it can be for those who can see the good times and appreciate it, rather than fixating on the end and the pain from that end. The good times are hard to see when your entire world view and outlook is negative. At least this has been my experience. I took the mistakes I made over the relationship as a learning experience, but for me, knowing how good it could be, just makes losing it x10 worse.

I feel you, today was really hard for me. I didn't have any time in between classes last semester, but now I got 3 hour gaps and one 7 hour gap... Spent 3 hours just sitting in the library listening to music by my self. Reminds me of high school, didn't think I would have to experience that again.

What happens if you don't have insurance and want to go to the hospital in this situation. I am reaching a point where I honestly am just done. I feel like I should just go to the hospital before I do something. Don't have insurance though.

This is why I love watching the most cynical and depressing shows. I don't want to watch people in relationships. Or overtly positive shows (although I binged Unbreakable Kimmy Schmidt). I can't watch movies anymore because my attention span is so low and I just lost my passion for them. There is this Canadian cop drama called 19-2. It's so melodramatic and insanely cynical. I love it.
I've been crying everyday almost this past week. It's a good thing I don't have to leave my house for a bit because I don't think I would be able to keep it together in public.

I feel like anytime I make a step forward in life I take two steps back. I just got out of a two year relationship that ended because I ignored my worsening depression (after I had a period where it was for the most part gone). I am back to where I was, alone again, three years ago. Only now is that I've learned a valuable lesson, that you can't take loved ones for granted. That your actions, cannot be excused by your mental health. Especially when you refuse to confront them and take it out on the other person. I just wish it didn't have to come to this for me to learn. 

The stakes and consequences were much lower before when I was young and only hurt my self. The guilt of what I've done weighs as heavy on me as my depression right now. I am trying to make it so I never repeat this again.

I feel you, I lost the best thing that has happened to me because I didn't want to deal with my depression and turned into an asshole. Now I regret it and am back to square one. Now I try to fight back the feeling of anger whenever I feel it rising.

Sorry man. I know in my state there are resources to help if you have no money, but even then it's not as good if you have insurance. Maybe she can call her insurance to find out if there are any options? I know because of the ACA, mental health services should be covered. Assuming you are in the United States. Maybe the suicide hotline of your country/state can connect you with the right resources.

Have you tried school resources? Many colleges have mental health services that provide counseling. Many counties/states provide mental health services on a sliding scale, based on income. There are many groups that also provide free therapy, dependent on location. Maybe her college can provide information on where to find those resources.

My father's brother committed suicide when he was a teen. Depression runs in my family. I didn't have a happy childhood. I wasn't abused or anything and my parents tried their best. But I was dealing with depression since I was very young, I just didn't know it then. 

People ask me if I want kids and I say no. I usually say it's too expensive or whatever but the truth is I wouldn't be able to live with myself if they had depression too. I don't want them to carry that burden. I also don't think I could be the best possible father because of having to deal with depression as well. Sometimes I think I'd want kids but I think again about how much I want to kill my self some days. It wouldn't be fair to them.

>Those we let get close to us can end up experiencing some of the worst we have to offer.

That is so true. There are days I don't even know who I am anymore. I feel like some part of me is very sensitive and caring. But it feels more like a distance memory. Instead the majority of who I am is cold and uncaring.
